s00-cup: A brushed-titanium chalice on a product-launch plinth in a wet concrete hall; a scanning laser line polishes across it; title POISONED CUPS glitches in with one faint green flicker. Spotless.
Sets the grammar: a beautiful polished object, a warning under the shine.
Cut on 'You' as the first word lands.
s01-poison: The chalice rim from above, perfect; on 'poison' the camera tilts over the rim: acid-green poison inside, glowing, oil slick and circuit debris.
Outside clean, inside poison: the song's first image, literally.
The green glow narrows to one lit point, top centre.
One green point of light, top centre.
s02-fringes: Opens on that green point: a fibre tip. Bundles of fibre-optic cable hang like prayer fringes, swinging; they fray and go dark one by one.
The last lit fibre becomes a vertical seam of light.
s03-tomb: The seam is the join in a seamless white server monolith; the crack opens along it: rusted racks, wiring like ribs, a skull-white fan hub.
Hard cut; the white fan hub matches the first white chrome bead of s04, same place in frame.
s04-prayers: Opens on a white chrome bead where the fan hub was: a smooth voice-assistant waveform of polished beads; they shatter into obsidian shards that fly like blades.
Blades rise on the chorus downbeat.
One shard flies into a server rack and strikes a spark.
s05-vipers: The shard's spark lands in a single server rack: chorus 1, one spark, black cable-vipers coiled below, unaware. BROOD OF VIPERS huge.
The warning is quiet the first time: one spark.
Smash to black on the last word.
Out of black, the spark's glow remains as one lit fibre.
s06-empire: That glowing fibre twists into a helix; white server towers trimmed in gold stack into a little skyline empire.
Twisting truth to build an empire.
The skyline completes on the cut.
The skyline in silhouette; its white towers match the white memorial pillars.
s07-prophets: Match on the towers: white memorial pillars with gold laurel and dead screens; blood-red coolant runs from their bases.
Red reaches the camera on the cut.
The red coolant runs into the dark under the vipers' cameras.
s08-see: Red coolant pooled under dark, cracked surveillance cameras (the vipers' own, pointed the wrong way). On 'I' a warm-white shaft of light falls from above (no lamp, no machine), stops on 'see' and finds one viper.
Their lenses are blind; the light is His.
The shaft holds on the one lit viper, then withdraws upward.
A close pattern of the viper's scales.
s09-gnat: The scale pattern resolves into a fine gold filter mesh under cold sodium work-light, catching one tiny glitch bug; a huge brass camel falls straight through.
Straining a gnat, swallowing a camel.
The camel hits the floor on the cut.
The brass camel hits a conveyor belt.
s10-loads: The camel lands on a conveyor: crates bound in straps lower onto it under sodium light; an empty white glove hovers a finger above the strap and pulls back on 'lift'.
They load others and won't lift a finger.
The crates land on the cut.
The white glove withdraws toward the titanium chalice on its plinth.
s11-widow: The glove withdraws past the titanium chalice; beside it a payment terminal with a smiling avatar whose eyes are blank bars smiles on 'smile'; on 'pays' two worn copper coins drop, clink on the chalice rim, spill a drop of green and roll off the plinth; the smile never changes.
Blind guides smile while the widow pays.
The coins roll out of frame.
s12-gate: The two coins roll to a stop under a gilt paywall gate whose price tag reads exactly two coins; on 'guard' it slams and the bolts shoot.
Selling the gate, then guarding it.
The lock snaps on the cut.
The gate slams; its laser grid turns to red heat.
s13-vipers2: The gate's red heat is fire: chorus 2, the fire has taken a whole row of racks; one viper rises to face it.
The warning grows: the fire is spreading.
Whip-pan off the viper onto its tongue's gleam, matching the wax seal.
s14-scrolls: A Scripture scroll unrolling on a glass lectern with a wax seal; on 'kiss' a lipstick kiss-print presses onto the seal; on 'liar' a forked tongue flicks out from under the scroll and the seal cracks.
Kissing the scrolls, calling God a liar.
The seal cracks on the cut.
The seal's crack becomes the crack in the white monolith.
s15-graves: The crack is the s03 monolith's crack again: robotic spray arms paint fresh white over it while LED incense smoke is pumped in; they win: the crack is sealed flawless and the smoke rolls over a beautiful, finished grave.
The lie perfected: the outside is spotless.
Smoke fills the frame on the cut.
Incense smoke fills the frame; a shaft of light cuts through it.
s16-see2: Through the smoke the warm shaft falls on the titanium chalice, polished and spotless; on 'see' the light passes through the metal like an X-ray and the acid-green inside shows through the wall. Lyric in dark ink off the lit area.
The shaft falls on a pair of gold goggles.
s17-we-see: The warm light falls on gold goggles with black lenses and dies on them; they reflect nothing; the camera pushes into one lens.
Claiming sight keeps them in darkness.
Into the black of the lens.
s18-clean: From the lens's darkness into a sterile clean room: a silver basin of clear water and the white gloves standing raised; the water clouds black.
Claiming to be clean with raised hands.
The gloves stay raised, palms up; the camera keeps moving.
s19-silver: Same room, same move: on 'palms' silver coins land and heap in the raised gloves' palms; on 'blood' red runs from the fingertips onto the white floor and spreads to the doorway.
Silver in their palms, blood on the floor.
s20-door: A tall doorway of warm light; an empty pair of white gloves stands in it, backlit, still on 'Won't walk in'; silhouettes of the poor on the near side; on 'poor' a glove swings the gold barrier arm down across the threshold, stopping a span from the nearest silhouette's outstretched hand.
They won't walk in or let the poor in: the barrier finishes the sentence.
Match cut on the warm light to fire.
s21-vipers3: Chorus 3: the whole hall burns; the server-tower empire is lit from below; vipers silhouetted.
The fire they were warned of, at full height.
s22-fall: The skyline empire of white towers; on 'Turn your hearts' one white glove at its foot turns palm-up toward a warm light for a beat; on 'proud dreams fall' the towers topple; on 'tire' the last slab settles, spent.
The call to repent, and the fall of what they built.
The last piece lands on the cut.
Gold trim scattered in the rubble.
s23-reed: Among the scattered gold trim in the rubble, one cracked green reed and a smouldering wick; warm light gathers round them: mercy, still gritty.
Mercy: I will never crush or kill.
The reed's warm light ends as one glint.
s24-bend: The glint catches the vipers, whole, rigid as steel, and the white gloves clenched; at their feet the fallen empire's concrete lies in broken stones.
If you won't bend: refusing to bend, refusing to lift, one image.
Hold on the rigid vipers, then cut on the downbeat.
The broken stones at their feet.
s25-stones: The empire's rubble round the unbending vipers lifts and burns with carved white light: the stones speak instead of them.
The stones will speak My will.
s26-clean-cup: The stones' light rises and arcs down into the chalice; the green burns away completely and the inside is bare bright metal lit from within, brighter than the outside ever was; the intro's scanning laser sweeps in, finds nothing to polish and switches off; caption 'First clean the inside of the cup' (2:36–2:42), then MATTHEW 23:26 (2:42–2:46); the push-out ends on the lit cup alone in the dark hall.
The answer to the whole song, caused on screen.
Fades out at the end, still moving.
